findings.window_definition: Stride-1 (history=30d, future=30d) pair from test set (start_idx=4540). N=1223 total windows.
findings.coverage_definition: Fraction of 750 points (30 timesteps x 25 cells) where GT is inside 90% CI (5th-95th percentile of 50 samples).

clustering.explanation: Stride-1 windows share 29/30 future days, so failures on specific market episodes affect all overlapping windows.

regime_breakdown.key_finding: Bad windows concentrate in CALM periods (13.7%) not turbulent (2.9%). Model overestimates calm-period predictability.

root_cause.explanation: Bad windows have 11% less ensemble spread but GT moves 56% faster. The model underestimates uncertainty during unexpectedly volatile calm periods.

ensemble_spread.note: Spread stays stable (no explosion or collapse), but does not grow monotonically as theory requires for longer horizons.

spatial_structure.smile_convexity: Decreases from 0.064 (30d) to 0.012 (252d), GT is 0.070-0.077. Model flattens smile at long horizons.

stationarity.note: Late-period daily change std is 16% of early-period = model becomes too stable at long horizons.

kurtosis.note: Heavy tails maintained at all horizons (log-space dynamics working).

cointegration_252d.note: SEVERE degradation at 252d. Model loses IV-EWMA relationship at long horizons.

cross_cell_correlation.note: Reasonable match at 252d (ratio 0.86), better than 30d suite.

findings.key_concern: Coverage drops from 82% at 30d to 30% at 180d. Spread stabilizes rather than growing, causing systematic undercoverage at long horizons. Cointegration collapses (15% vs GT 98%).

metric_a_gram_eff_rank.description: K x K Gram matrix of ensemble members (what training DPP loss optimizes)
metric_a_gram_eff_rank.note: DPP loss successfully increases Gram eff_rank by +24%.

metric_b_daily_change_corr_eff_rank.description: 25x25 correlation matrix of daily changes across cells (what test Suite 9 measures)
metric_b_daily_change_corr_eff_rank.note: Only +8% improvement in test metric despite +24% in training metric.

per_member_structure.note: Per-member correlation structure barely changed. All members have rank ~1.5, confirming rank-1 attractor within each member.

cross_member_diversity.note: DPP successfully halved cross-member correlation (members are more diverse). But this diversity is along PC1, not across cells.

findings.explanation: The DPP loss diversifies ensemble MEMBERS (makes them different from each other in the T*H*W output space). But it does NOT change the WITHIN-member factor structure. Each individual member still has rank-1 cell correlation (all 25 cells move together). The test suite measures the 25x25 cell correlation matrix using individual sample trajectories, so it sees the within-member structure. DPP creates members that are different along the dominant PC1 axis, which increases Gram rank but leaves the per-trajectory cell correlation virtually unchanged.

eigenvalue_evidence.note: GT has 5+ meaningful eigenvalues. Both models are dominated by eigenvalue 1 (93% and 91% PC1 variance vs GT 61%). The DPP slightly reduced PC1 dominance (93% -> 91%) but nowhere near GT's 61%.

findings.implication: To improve Suite 9, need a loss that directly targets within-member cell correlation structure (e.g., variogram score, correlation matching loss, or factor-structured noise injection). DPP alone cannot solve rank-1.
